 iPhone Duo 2 could get Face ID under the display
 By 
 Akarsh Rasik 
 Published: October 22, 2026 
 Share 
 2 Min Read 
 Image Credits: Apple 
 SHARE 
 Highlights 
 Apple is testing under-display Face ID for the iPhone Duo 2.
 A telephoto camera could arrive in a future iPhone Duo model.
 Apple is also considering adding an Action button to its foldable iPhone.
 Apple could bring Face ID to its next foldable iPhone, as the company is reportedly testing the feature on iPhone Duo 2 prototypes. The technology would sit beneath the display and allow users to unlock the phone using facial recognition rather than a fingerprint sensor.
 Apple working on Face ID for iPhone Duo 2
 The current iPhone Duo uses a fingerprint sensor built into the side button. One reason for this choice is the phone’s slim design, which leaves less room for the hardware needed for Face ID.
 Apple is now testing whether these components can fit beneath the display. If the technology works as expected, the next model could offer facial recognition without requiring a visible sensor cutout. However, Apple has not made a final decision, so the feature could still change before the phone reaches the market.
 More changes could be on the way
 Face ID is not the only change being discussed for future iPhone Duo models. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman has previously reported that Apple could add a dedicated telephoto camera to a later version of the device.
 Apple is also considering an Action button, which is already available on other iPhone models. It lets users quickly access features such as the camera or flashlight. Whether these upgrades will arrive with the iPhone Duo 2 or a later model remains unclear.

 What happens next?
 For now, Apple seems to be exploring multiple ways to improve its foldable iPhone. Under-display Face ID could be a useful addition, especially for users who prefer facial recognition over a fingerprint sensor.
 Still, the company has not confirmed the phone’s final features or launch details. More information is needed to know which of these changes will make it into the next model.
